messages.subject: JavaGD R 2.13.0 Windows binary on CRAN is missing a 64-bit DLL
messages.subject_clean: JavaGD R 2.13.0 Windows binary on CRAN is missing a 64-bit DLL
messages.body_plain:
This is just a heads-up to JavaGD/JGR users on Windows that use 64-bit R: the current JavaGD binary on CRAN is missing 64-bit DLLs, so use

install.packages("JavaGD",,"http://rforge.net")

instead. The symptom with the CRAN binary is that you'll see:

> Loading required package: JavaGD
> Error in library.dynam("WinRegistry", pkgname, libname) :
>   DLL 'WinRegistry' not found: maybe not installed for this architecture?
> Error: package 'JavaGD' could not be loaded

In general, if you have issues with 64-bit on Windows, use RForge binaries, they are usually more complete since they use full merge of 32 and 64-bit packages (as opposed to --libs-only which is the default way in R and doesn't merge all files).

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: GUI Experience - Box Plots
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

This is to share my experience of using GUI's for using various
Quality Management/Assurance tools.
A few days back, I had I had written a mail about Box plots and
received some very good suggestions, including that for simple
scripts.  Thanks everybody for the same.

Based on the suggestions, I am trying three GUI's:  R Commander,
JGR-Deducer combination and RKward.

For Box Plots, I found the JGR-Deducer combination the best choice.

I could not get box plots - Factors and Dodging - in R Commander and
RKward, though the reply on RKward mailing list suggests that the
newer version of RKward should solve the problem.

Thank you everybody for all the help.  I'll be asking questions about
various tools that I would like to deploy through GUI's for R.  I'll
also be sharing my experiences.

Vikas Garud

messages.subject: Pareto Analysis using GUI
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am exploring GUI's for doing Quality
Management/Assurance/Improvement activities and this is another mail
in series!

Focus of this mail is Pareto Analysis for following data (Truncated):
Date	Defect code	Operator	Shift	Machine	Cost - Internal	Cost -
External	Cost - Total
8-Jun-2011	410	Joe	1	AAA	5	50	55
8-Jun-2011	465	Joe	1	AAA	1.5	25	26.5
8-Jun-2011	412	Joe	1	AAA	1.5	10	11.5
8-Jun-2011	410	Joe	1	AAA	5	50	55
8-Jun-2011	218	Joe	1	AAA	1	10	11
8-Jun-2011	440	Joe	1	AAA	1	10	11
8-Jun-2011	410	Joe	1	AAA	5	50	55
8-Jun-2011	413	Joe	1	AAA	0.5	5	5.5
8-Jun-2011	410	Joe	1	AAA	5	50	55
8-Jun-2011	465	Moe	1	BBB	1.5	25	26.5
8-Jun-2011	410	Moe	1	BBB	5	50	55
8-Jun-2011	412	Moe	1	BBB	1.5	10	11.5
8-Jun-2011	841	Moe	1	BBB	0.5	5	5.5
8-Jun-2011	410	Moe	1	BBB	5	50	55
8-Jun-2011	413	Moe	1	BBB	0.5	5	5.5
8-Jun-2011	410	Moe	1	BBB	5	50	55
8-Jun-2011	413	Moe	1	BBB	0.5	5	5.5
8-Jun-2011	465	Moe	1	BBB	1.5	25	26.5
8-Jun-2011	410	Moe	1	BBB	5	50	55

In all cases, the qcc package is loaded.

The data in this example to demonstrate Pareto Chart contains 8 defect
codes and it is possible to make sense of the plot.  Some real data
contains hundreds of records.  (There is file, somewhere on the
internet - sorry, I could not find the link - CFHPareto.xls containing
11099 records in 37 defect codes.)  Doing a Pareto Analysis with all
categories is not of practical use, the focus is on vital few, the
useful many's clutter the plot area and the legends can not be read.
For such data, I would like to club categories beyond, say, 80% in
cumulative total, to be clubbed in "Others".    Is it possible?  How?

Using JGR-Deducer, I could not get any option for plotting Pareto
chart.  The "Frequencies" under the "Analysis" menu computed the
number of times a particular defect code occurs.  This could be used
for plotting Bar chart - though not Pareto chart with the lines above
the bars.  However, I could not sort the output table.  I could also
not get any way to compute values for plotting bar plot of defect
codes based on total cost.  Is there a way to accomplish Pareto Chart,
may be through couple of stages?

Any help is appreciated.

Regards
Vikas Garud

messages.body_plain:
Unfortunately you cut out the thread, so it took me a while to track down what you are really talking about by going back in the posts and replies.

First, you quoted a completely irrelevant thread. Second, your subject is completely irrelevant to what you were asking (if not, explain). And, finally, if you have 32-bit R then the whole question is moot since you have to use 32-bit Java in that case. Now to your question out of context:

On Jun 4, 2011, at 9:57 AM, Pete Shell wrote:

> 
> 
> Simon Urbanek <simon.urbanek <at> r-project.org> writes:
> 
> ....
>>> 
>>> If that's the case, make sure you use the 64-bit version of JRI.DLL (either 
> add x64 to the library path or
>> copy the 64-bit version down).
>>> 
>>> Cheers,
>>> Simon
>>> 
> 
> 
> I have the same problem on my 64-bit Windows 7 machine but there is no x64 folder for R. How do I get the 64-bit version of JRI.dll? If somebody could give me a specific web site or instructions that would be really helpful.
> 

If you don't have x64 folders in R then you have 32-bit R so you can't use 64-bit JRI - with 32-bit R you have to use 32-bit JRI and 32-bit Java. If you want 64-bit R, download latest R from CRAN.

If you have x64 folders in R (i.e., your R is 64-bit), but install.packages doesn't give you x64 folder in rJava/JRI then use
install.packages("rJava",,"http://rforge.net")
and make sure you have installed 64-bit Java.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am trying to have javaGD embedded in a custom frame (not in default JavaGD()).

Following instructions in this mailing list (2006: Plotting to
JGDPanel) or from elsewhere:
http://www.algorithm-forge.com/techblog/2010/07/using-javagd-in-java-applications/
http://www.wojtek.njh6.de/Ddocs/Djri/jri.html

MyJavaGD.class is exactly the same as JavaGD.class except:
engine.eval(".setenv(\"JAVAGD_CLASS_NAME\"=\"MyJavaGD\")");

Problem 1) If outside of /org/rosuda/javaGD, and using import
org.rosuda.javaGD.*;, MyJavaGD.class does not compile:

devNr is not public in org.rosuda.javaGD.GDInterface; cannot be
accessed from outside package

Problem 2) If placing inside /org/rosuda, the following exception occurs:

Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: MyJavaGD
	at org.rosuda.JRI.Rengine.rniEval(Native Method)
	at org.rosuda.JRI.Rengine.eval(Rengine.java:549)
	at org.rosuda.JRI.Rengine.eval(Rengine.java:527)
	at JavaGDExample.main(JavaGDExample.java:35)
Caused by: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: MyJavaGD
	at java.net.URLClassLoader$1.run(URLClassLoader.java:217)
	at java.security.AccessController.doPrivileged(Native Method)
	at java.net.URLClassLoader.findClass(URLClassLoader.java:205)
	at java.lang.ClassLoader.loadClass(ClassLoader.java:321)
	at sun.misc.Launcher$AppClassLoader.loadClass(Launcher.java:294)
	at java.lang.ClassLoader.loadClass(ClassLoader.java:266)

The frame has ' JavaGD (2) *active*' as title, which indicates the use
of default JavaGD().

Thank you in advance for hints, best regarrds.

Fran,ois
